newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pound climbs vs yen on Eurotunnel loans, UK data.
newsitem.headline: Pound climbs vs yen on Eurotunnel loans, UK data.

text.p: The pound's recent rise against the yen is partly due to speculation that Japanese banks are making provisions in sterling in order to write off their loans to Eurotunnel SA /Eurotunnel Plc, bankers said on Wednesday.
A group of about 36 Japanese banks hold around 1.63 billion pounds worth of Eurotunnel's eight billion pounds in junior-ranked debt, banking sources in Tokyo said.

"Japanese banks are keen to buy sterling to make provisions to write off their loans to Eurotunnel before they close their books," said Noriyuki Mizukami, head of treasury sales at National Westminster Bank in Tokyo.
Japan's financial year ends on March 31.

Some bankers estimated that about half of their loan exposure, or around 815 million pounds worth of debt, to the troubled Anglo-French tunnel operator had already been written off after they put aside about 30 to 50 percent in provisions.

If the banks which had not put aside pounds were to do so, the amount they would need to buy would be from around 244.5 million pounds to as much as 407.5 million pounds, Japanese banking sources said.
But since some of the banks are believed to have sold their Eurotunnel loans in the secondary market, the actual amount of pounds they need could be much smaller.
Sterling was quoted at 200.73/85 yen at 0740 GMT on Wednesday, up sharply from 196.95 yen at the Tokyo opening on Monday.

One British bank dealer in Tokyo said that while there was vague market talk of the possible purchase of as much as 400 million pounds on Wednesday, partly from Japanese banks' settlements related to outstanding loans to Eurotunnel, he felt the total amount was likely to be closer to 150 million pounds.
He added that sterling sales ahead of the March 31 corporate book closing were likely to cancel out all but around 20 million to 30 million pounds of this purchase, minimising the impact.
In addition to the Eurotunnel factor, news of healthy economic growth in Britain earlier this week has been sparking sterling purchases, currency dealers said.

The Office for National Statistics in Britain said on Monday that revised fourth-quarter gross domestic product data showed growth of 0.8 percent from the previous quarter and 2.6 percent year-on-year. On the top of that, fourth-quarter current account data showed a surplus of 873 million pounds against a forecast of 400,000 pounds shortfall.

Those strong figures led to market expectations that Britain might be prepared to raise its interest rates even before the May 1 general election, which also helped push sterling up against major currencies, dealers said.

"Until recently, traders were cautious about buying pounds before the election. But if they begin to cover their short positions more aggressively now, a rise to 210 yen is possible by the end of April," said National Westminster's Mizukami.
